result.note: p_mw is each load's demand at the operating point the network is at now (the simulation clock's moment, `operating_point`), not a rating. A category the network does not state can be declared by the operator (declare_network_facts, loads); until then it is unknown — never guessed.

result.from: inferred from the topology as switched now: the first line after the last transformer on the route from the external grid; only where the voltage level is radial

category.from: the network does not say what kind of demand this is

p.from: Bus 11's consumption in the synthetic data

q.from: P·tan(acos 0.97) — the load power factor (the network's profile); not in the data

kv.from: the bus's nominal voltage in the network

substation.from: buses joined by transformers or bus couplers; a single bus is a substation of its own

feeder.from: inferred from the topology as switched now: the first line after the last transformer on the route from the external grid; only where the voltage level is radial

supply.from: inferred from the topology as switched now: the shortest route by number of branches from an external grid; the feeder is the first line after the last transformer on it

without_it.from: topology only: the buses that lose every connection to an external grid (no power flow run); the load is their demand at the network's current operating point
open_ties_that_could_restore: Line 11-4 | Bus 11 -> Bus 4 [L13] (switch S3, open at Bus 4)

assistant:
Load R11 is supplied by the **Line 1-2 feeder** (inferred from the topology as currently switched).

The inferred route from the external grid is: **Trafo 0-1**, then **Line 1-2**, **Line 2-3**, **Line 3-8**, **Line 8-9**, **Line 9-10**, and **Line 10-11**. There is also a tie, **Line 11-4**, but it is open at Bus 4.
